Replaced CPU s=1 PU200 budget: T5 33 + pT5 26 + pT3 44 + TC 116 = 219 ms, plus the T4 stage and the plsembdnn share of pLS ingestion (~20-40 ms) — roughly 240-260 ms in scope.

New stages (CPU, assuming ~5 GFLOP/s effective on the auto-vectorized MLP loops, which matches the measured t5dnn-dominated costs today):
- K1 CSR: ~2e6 ops -> 1-2 ms. K2 sort: 1e5 keys -> ~1 ms.
- K3+K4 following: seeds ~6e4 (Wave 1) + ~4e4 (Wave 2, post-claim). Fake-dominated seeds terminate in ~1 step with ~3 pregated candidates; real seeds (~1e4) run ~5 steps x B=2 x ~3 scored candidates. ExtendNet calls ~ 6e5-1.2e6 x 1.1k FLOP ~ 0.7-1.3 GFLOP -> 50-100 ms including pregate loads. TrackNet: ~1e5 x 2.4k -> ~10 ms.
- K5 arbitration: ~3e6 atomic/int ops -> ~2 ms (vs the ~60 ms dedup share of today's TC stage).
- K6+K7 pixel: grid build O(nPLS) ~ 2 ms; attach pairs ~ nTracks(5e3) x ~20 + nPLS(5e4) x ~4 stub candidates ~ 3e5 net calls x 0.9k -> ~10-15 ms (vs 70 ms pT3+pT5 today, and no host superbin loops).
- K8 assembly: ~5 ms.
Total: **~90-140 ms vs 240-260 ms** — a ~2x margin on the replaced scope, so C5 holds even if the following estimate is 50% low. Honest uncertainties: the fake-seed step-1 termination rate (if fakes survive 3 steps, following triples to ~150-300 ms and the margin narrows to ~parity) and Wave-2 seed count after claiming; both are measurable in week-1 prototypes (Section 9).

GPU: today's 1.9 ms/event is bounded by the T5 dense path (one 256-thread block owning ~1.6e8 FLOPs per hot module pair, twice) and single-thread-serial dedup chunks. Following is one warp per seed, embarrassingly parallel, ~1.3 GFLOP total — microseconds of arithmetic on an L40; realistic cost is launch/divergence-bound, ~0.3-0.6 ms for K3/K4, with kernel count nearly halved and 6 host round-trips removed (biggest GPU-specific win: no superbin host loops, no T5-count sync). Jet-core scaling (C1): current dense module pair ~3.2e8 FLOPs serialized on one block x2 kernels + ~1e9 dedup int-ops; new core cost ~2e3 Wave-1 seeds x 5 x 2 x (50-candidate pregate at 10 FLOPs + 3 net calls) ~ 1e7 pregate FLOPs + 6e4 net calls ~ 8e7 FLOPs, spread over 2e3 independent warps. That is ~50x less arithmetic and ~2000x more parallelism at the point where the current code serializes; the exponent argument (h^6 -> h^4 visits, h^5 -> h^3 expensive-constant) is in Section 1.

## 5. DISPLACED ARGUMENT

The 31.2% T3->T5 kill is caused by three deleted things: (a) t5dnn as the unconditional first gate, with 4 raw IP-referenced first-hit coordinates and WPs tuned on prompt-dominated samples; (b) the dBeta selectors, whose betaIn/betaOut are defined against beamline-referenced segment alphas and whose cut includes an explicit luminous-region term (kDeltaZLum) — a hard IP assumption applied twice per T5; (c) prompt-derived RZ region thresholds. In the follower, the entire critical selection path is residual-based: every gating quantity is a difference between the candidate and a helix fitted through the track's *own* hits, so a vxy=10 cm track and a prompt track present statistically identical inputs step-by-step. The only origin-adjacent inputs are (r,z) module conditioning (ExtendNet 10-11) and the seed's t3dnn scores (TrackNet); both are ablation-monitored, and neither can express "does not point at the IP" without combining with features we do not provide (absolute phi, position eta).

pLS-less population: Wave-2 seeding from the T4 region plus *inward* extension covers tracks entering at L2-L4; 4-layer tracks are first-class TCs gated only by theta_accept(4), replacing today's requirement that a T4 be DNN-classified displaced AND pass an explicitly IP-referenced dxy anti-prompt veto — that veto existed to suppress prompt T4 duplicates of T5s, a job K5 arbitration now does by hit claiming without any IP reference. Track length +displaced synergy: today +1.4% displaced eff came from grafting duplicate-T5 layers; the follower gets those layers directly (Section 6).

Training strategy: 50% PU200 prompt / 50% displaced-enriched (displaced-vertex particle guns flat in vxy 0-50 cm plus SUSY/HNL-type samples), loss reweighted so both populations contribute equally per dxy decade. Labels are **track-level, not object-level** (the forensic finding on plsembdnn showed object-level sim-matching produced a network worse than physics chi2 for the actual TC-level task): a step candidate is positive iff its MD belongs to the same sim track that majority-owns the seed; a track is positive iff >=75% of its hits belong to one reconstructible sim track — the same matching definition used by the TC-level efficiency harness, so the network optimizes the deployed metric. Training gates: per-dxy-bin efficiency curves (0-1, 1-5, 5-10, 10-20, 20+ cm) must dominate the current baseline before any WP is frozen; an ablation run with features 10-11 removed bounds the IP leakage (if removing them costs <0.3% prompt eff, ship without them).

Why >= today: the surviving displaced acceptance today is 46.8% after the module map, T3 cuts, t5dnn, dBeta, RZ, and prompt WPs each take bites; this design removes every post-T3 bite except a single learned accept trained explicitly half-displaced, and adds inward extension and cap-free 4-layer acceptance that today's T4 path (displaced-only classification + dxy veto + last-priority crosscleaning against everything) suppresses.

## 6. TRACK LENGTH

Following does not stop at 5 layers: S=9 steps over logical layers 1-11 plus inward extension means a track's length is whatever the detector offers — 6-7-layer tracks arise on the first pass instead of via ExtendT5FromDupT5's graft-from-duplicates (capped at +2 layers and 40 compat modules, both deleted). K5 arbitration inherits today's longer-track-wins tiebreak via the (score|length) priority key. The TC SoA's 13 positional layer slots already accommodate 11 OT layers + 2 pixel. Expected outcome: strictly longer mean track length than today, since today's extension only fires when a near-duplicate T5 happens to exist and share >=8/10 hits, while the follower extends whenever one MD continuation clears a learned gate; C6 is met with margin, verified by the nLayers distribution comparison in every phase (Section 10).

## 7. PIXEL SIDE

Superbin maps deleted. K6 builds one device (eta,phi) grid (64x64 cells) over pLS directions: count/prefix/fill CSR, O(nPLS), one thread per pLS; ~3 ms CPU at 1e5 pLS, and it uses seed *direction* parameters that pLS legitimately carry. K7 has two symmetric passes: (i) track-centric — each accepted OT track propagates its inner state inward, reads the 3x3 grid neighborhood (~nPLS/4096 x 9 ~ 20-200 candidates in jets), runs PixelAttachNet on each: 5e3 tracks x ~30 = 1.5e5 calls; (ii) stub-centric — 3-layer stubs (followed seeds that stopped at 3 layers with score above a low floor, the pT3-equivalent population) are grid-hashed the same way and matched from the pLS side: ~5e4 pLS x ~4 = 2e5 calls. Total ~3.5e5 x 0.9k FLOP ~ 0.3 GFLOP -> 10-15 ms CPU at the 1e5-pLS extreme, linear in nPLS with a small constant — timing-competitive against today's 70 ms pT3+pT5 with their two host superbin loops, and it scales to O(100k) pLS because candidates per object are grid-bounded, not map-fanout-bounded. No 5000/15000 global caps: merged-track storage is bounded by nTracks and nStub attach acceptance, allocated dynamically like every other collection. The "significant fraction of unmatchable pLSs" map-coverage hole (LSTEvent.dev.cc:838 comment) disappears — grid coverage is total.

## 8. TRAINING & DEPLOYMENT

Pipeline: standalone `-d` build writes follower training branches (per-step candidate features + sim labels) the same way t4dnn's ntuple branches work today; a teacher pass runs the follower with truth-guided beam (oracle) to generate balanced positive/negative step samples including hard negatives (in-cone wrong-track continuations). Train ExtendNet on step labels, TrackNet on completed-track labels, PixelAttachNet on (pLS, track) sim-pair labels — all with the track-level definitions of Section 5. Calibration: each net's output is Platt-scaled so thresholds are stable percentiles; the 8 scalar WPs are set once from efficiency targets (e.g. theta_extend at 99.5% per-step true-continuation efficiency; theta_accept(nLayers) at the fake-rate parity point vs baseline) — no eta/pt binning, since the nets condition on the relevant variables internally. Retraining story: one script regenerates ntuples, retrains 3 nets (~minutes at these sizes), re-emits the three weight headers (same HOST_DEVICE_CONSTANT mechanism as today) and 8 scalars; geometry changes require only retracing upstream maps and rerunning it. Weekly-retrain-capable, versus today's 6 nets and 10 hand-frozen tables.

## 9. RISK REGISTER

1. **Fake seeds don't die in ~1 step, blowing the CPU budget.** Early measurement: instrument step-count distribution on 10 PU200 events with an untrained (physics-window) gate. Kill criterion: mean steps per fake seed > 2.5 after training implies following > 250 ms; mitigate with a stronger pregate (distilled 1-layer linear scorer, ~30 FLOPs) or seed prefilter on t3 fakeScore. 
2. **Beam B=2 loses real tracks at in-core branch points.** Oracle study first (truth-guided follower ceiling on PU200 + jet samples must be >= baseline eff - 0.2% at B=2); if only B=4 closes it, timing doubles — kill and fall back to hybrid (follower for non-dense, current path for dense modules).
3. **4-layer acceptance without the IP dxy veto floods fakes.** Measurable per-length fake rate in phase 3; mitigate with theta_accept(4) tightening or (worst case) reinstating displaced-only 4-layer acceptance via the TrackNet inputs — still no dxy feature.
4. **Hit-claim arbitration kills legitimately hit-sharing dense-core tracks.** Validate the 0.6 unclaimed-fraction threshold against today's dup definitions on jet-enriched samples; kill criterion: duplicate rate > baseline or in-jet eff drop > 0.3%; mitigation: per-layer (not per-hit) claiming, which tolerates shared single hits.
5. **IP leakage through (r,z) conditioning re-creates the displaced kill.** The Section 5 ablation is the gate: displaced eff per dxy bin must be flat-or-better vs baseline both with and without features 10-11; if the with-features net shows a dxy-correlated deficit, ship the ablated net (bounded cost measured up front).

## 10. MIGRATION PATH

**Phase 1 — Arbitration replaces the dedup/crossclean cascade (no new NNs).** Implement K5 propose-verify hit claiming over today's existing T5/T4/pT3/pT5 objects, replacing RemoveDupQuintupletsBeforeTC, both T4 dedups, and the CrossClean cascade's hit-based parts. Independently landable; validated with the standard createPerfNumDenHists / lst_plot_performance --compare harness plus lst_timing; expected TC-stage win ~60-90 ms CPU and removal of the ~1e9-op serial chunks on GPU. De-risks the arbitration machinery.

**Phase 2 — Grid attach replaces the superbin maps.** K6/K7 with PixelAttachNet attach pLS to today's T5s (pT5-equivalent) and T3s (pT3-equivalent), deleting the 12 map files, the host superbin loops, pt3dnn, plsembdnn, and the 5000/15000 caps. Same object outputs, drop-in comparable; jets are the acceptance test (cap-loss recovery should show up as in-jet eff gain).

**Phase 3 — Follower replaces T5+T4 builders.** K1-K4 produce OT tracks consumed by the phase-1 arbitration and phase-2 attach; delete both T5 count/create kernels, ExtendT5FromDupT5, the T4 stage, t5dnn, t5embdnn, t4dnn and all their tables. Baseline comparison at full-chain level (eff/fake/dup/length vs dxy, pT, eta; per-stage timing both backends); the oracle and step-count studies from Section 9 gate entry.

**Phase 4 — Unification.** Stub-based pT3-equivalents, single TC assembly, removal of remaining legacy thresholds, end-to-end retrain of the three nets on the final pipeline, WP freeze from the 8-scalar calibration. Each phase leaves the repo shippable and benchmarked against the previous one; no big-bang step exists.

judges.completeness:
1. **Legitimate hit sharing is structurally forbidden by all four designs.** Design 0's union-find partitions T3s into disjoint components, Design 1's PathGrow allows "a T3 joins at most one chain," Design 2's K14 kills one of any pair sharing >=0.6 hits, and Design 3's arbitration claims MDs exclusively — yet photon conversions, boosted tau three-prongs, and close-by tracks in a single 2S module (strips cannot separate them in z) genuinely share hits. Today's cascade at least emits both duplicates and lets downstream resolve; all four replace that with winner-take-all. Suggestion: measure the sim-level rate of distinct reconstructible tracks sharing >=2 MDs (conversions and dense cores) and add an explicit "shared-hit exemption" (per-layer claiming, or allow a T3/MD to be a member of up to 2 components) with a conversion-sample efficiency gate.

2. **Non-constant curvature (electron bremsstrahlung, decays-in-flight) breaks every design's core cheap gate.** All four adopt |delta(1/R)| and |delta(tanLambda)| consistency windows between inner and outer T3s/steps as the first origin-free filter — but electrons systematically lose energy so curvature grows along the trajectory, and kaon/pion decays-in-flight produce helix kinks; both violate constant-kappa exactly where the current dBeta machinery had tolerance built in. Neither the brief nor any design mentions electrons once. Suggestion: make the curvature window asymmetric (allow |kappa_out| > |kappa_in| by a brem-shaped tail) or add a material-conditioned width, and add electron-gun and displaced-kaon samples to every kill-criterion suite.

3. **Curvature-sign/charge-equality gates are unreliable exactly in the C1 target (TeV jet cores).** Designs 0/1/2 all place charge-sign or curvature-sign agreement as the first 1-op edge cut, but at pT >~ 100 GeV the 3-hit sagitta (~50 um over a 20 cm chord) is comparable to 2S hit resolution, so the fitted sign is near-random and the gate rejects ~50% of true high-pT edges — precisely the high-pT dijet population the jet-core constraint is about. Suggestion: bypass sign/curvature-difference gates whenever |kappa| is below a resolution-derived threshold (a straightness test), and include sign-flip rate vs pT in the phase-1 edge-ROC measurement.

4. **Loopers and low-pT curl-back violate the monotonic-layer assumption everywhere.** At the 0.8 GeV default cut a track's helix radius is ~70 cm, so sub-GeV tracks curl inside the OT, revisit layers at different phi, and produce z-reversing segments; all four designs (chains ordered by logical layer, "extend forward at last MD," E1/E2 direction conventions) inherit strict outward progression from the current code, and the forensic study never scanned for it. Suggestion: quantify the 0.8-1.5 GeV curl-back sim population; either declare it out of acceptance with a measured number, or permit same-layer-revisit edges as a distinct edge flavor in the graph designs.

5. **The brief's "from T3s onward" scope makes every displaced and timing claim Amdahl-capped by unexamined upstream stages.** The user's own research notes that module map, segment cuts, AND triplet cuts are all IP-tuned, yet all four keep the T3 pointing/RZ constraints untouched (Design 0 explicitly "kept as-is"); meanwhile pLS ingestion (334 ms), MD (91 ms), and LS (76 ms) dwarf the redesigned stages, so post-redesign the pipeline optimum shifts wholly upstream and event-level speedup saturates near 1.5-2x. Suggestion: add a stage-0 measurement of displaced loss and time attributable to MD/LS/T3/pLS cuts so the four proposals' ceilings (and the 46.8% baseline comparisons) are stated against the true upstream bound.

6. **No determinism/reproducibility specification for HLT.** Design 1's K4 accumulates float messages with atomics (order-dependent sums), Design 0's asynchronous union-find and K6 merges are schedule-dependent, and mutual-best/min-d2 selections have unhandled score ties; run-to-run and CPU-vs-GPU reproducibility — a real requirement for trigger validation — appears in no design and no brief constraint. Suggestion: require bitwise run-to-run determinism as a land criterion, use ordered segmented reductions (CSR-ordered, not atomic-float) and total-order tie-break keys (score|index) in every arbitration.

7. **Deleting fixed caps without a bounded-memory story is an HLT liability.** All four celebrate removing the 5000/15000 caps in favor of exact-count dynamic allocation, but at HLT with 8 concurrent streams a pathological event (noise burst, beam splash) can then demand unbounded device memory and fail an allocation mid-fill — the ugly caps are currently the worst-case bound. Suggestion: retain per-collection safety ceilings sized from a measured 99.99th-percentile occupancy, with overflow counters exported to DQM rather than silent truncation, plus a per-stream memory budget analysis.

8. **ROCm is absent from all four designs and the brief.** Design 3 builds on one-warp-per-seed with warp reductions (wavefront 64 on AMD, 32 on NVIDIA), Design 1 proposes warp-aggregated atomics, Design 0 leans on ECL-CC atomic idioms benchmarked on CUDA — none states a ROCm validation plan even though LSTCore ships a ROCm backend and Alpaka does not magically equalize atomic throughput or warp-width assumptions. Suggestion: add a ROCm build+physics-parity gate to every phase and forbid warp-width-dependent algorithms (or template them on `alpaka::warp::getSize`).

9. **All four inherit "NN weights as compiled headers" and even advertise it.** Weights live in `src/alpaka/*NetworkWeights.h` as HOST_DEVICE_CONSTANT arrays, so every alignment-era or ptCut retrain requires a CMSSW release rebuild instead of a conditions update — the designs increase retraining cadence (contrastive embeddings, threshold recalibration) while keeping the delivery mechanism least suited to it. Suggestion: move weights and the scalar thresholds into the EventSetup path that already exists (`LSTESData`), versioned through the conditions DB like the pixel maps' successor data.

10. **The whole exercise is MC-only: no data-driven validation, no domain-shift robustness.** Training and every kill criterion use sim labels; nothing addresses real-data misalignment, dead/noisy modules, beamspot drift (pLS dxy/dz features are beamspot-referenced), or how efficiency will be measured where sim truth doesn't exist — only Design 1 gestures at score-drift DQM. Suggestion: specify data-driven efficiency measurements (Z->mumu tag-and-probe, K_S/Lambda displaced vertices), train with misalignment/dead-channel/beamspot-variation augmentation, and define per-run score-distribution monitoring for all learned gates.

11. **Detector-aging and hit-inefficiency robustness is untested.** All designs feature layer-gap tolerance as an input, but chains/paths/components still assume that consecutive-layer MDs exist; a dead PS module or HL-LHC-aged efficiency loss turns a 5-layer track into two fragments, and no training mix includes realistic bad-channel maps. Suggestion: add a killed-module stress test (randomly disable 1-2% of modules) to the validation matrix and train with dropout-style hit removal.

12. **All timing arguments are means; HLT budgets are tails.** Every design quotes average ms/event at PU200 and worst-case h-scaling arguments, but none commits to a latency-distribution target (99th-percentile event, straggler streams), which is what actually determines HLT farm sizing — and irregular kernels (union-find, beams, dynamic edge counts) typically widen tails even when they improve means. Suggestion: make the 99th-percentile event time on a jet-enriched skim a first-class land criterion alongside the mean.

13. **Several cheap classical ideas appear in none of the four.** Nobody proposes: per-module phi-sorted sweeps (sorting hits/T3s once and replacing pair scans with bounded-window merges — a non-NN fix to the same O(h^2) scans), learned or historical occupancy prediction to pre-size allocations and delete the count-pass/host-sync entirely, curvature-binned (stub-bend-binned) processing that exploits the pT-module bend already encoded in MD dPhiChange as a partition key, or an explicit two-pass prompt-then-displaced strategy (reconstruct prompt tightly, subtract claimed hits, run a looser displaced pass on the residual — Design 3's waves are region-based, not origin-based). Suggestion: prototype the sorted-sweep and prompt-subtract variants as cheap baselines before committing to embedding/GNN infrastructure; they de-risk the NN bets.

14. **The 2S/PS distinction is only ever a feature, never a structure.** PS modules give ~mm z precision while 2S barrel z is ~cm-scale, yet all four feed uniform |delta tanLambda| and rz-residual windows over both — a tanLambda window computed from 2S-only hits is noise, and conversely PS-anchored fits could carry the rz decision alone. Suggestion: make rz windows and fit weights explicitly resolution-weighted per module class (inverse-variance in the incremental fits), and consider requiring at least one PS anchor before spending NN evaluations on an rz-marginal candidate.

15. **Downstream CMSSW contract and final-fit interaction are hand-waved.** All designs emit "T5-like/pT5-like" types, but the downstream chain (LSTObjType semantics in `RecoTracker/LST`, seed construction, the CKF final fit, and post-LST duplicate cleaning/quality MVAs) consumes today's object taxonomy and hit-count profiles; aggressive hit grafting (Design 0 K9's 11-layer components, Design 2 K14 grafts) changes outlier profiles the final fit was never validated against, and variable-length chains blur the pT5>pT3>T5 priority the downstream cleaner assumes. Suggestion: add an explicit phase gate running the full CMSSW workflow (24834.703/.704) through final fit with hit-residual and MVA-score distributions compared, not just MTV efficiency.

16. **Truth-definition circularity in all training plans.** Every design trains and calibrates against the existing MTV-style ">=75% hit match" criterion, which itself under-credits shared-hit tracks, short displaced stubs, and merged-core pairs — so the learned pipelines will optimize toward the metric's blind spots (e.g., dropping a legitimate second track whose hits are majority-shared), and no design questions the label definition it inherits. Suggestion: audit the matching criterion on the specific new failure modes (fragmentation, merges, shared-hit pairs) and report a second, hit-purity-independent metric (sim-track find rate at any purity) in all A/B comparisons.
